title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
subtitle: Garlic and chilli spaghetti
excerpt: One of the simplest pasta dishes in the Italian repertoire, made from nothing but garlic, olive oil, chilli, and pasta water. The trick is getting the garlic golden without burning it. Master that and the rest follows in minutes.
sourceNotes: A Roman and Neapolitan staple, spaghetti aglio e olio is one of the foundational recipes of Italian cucina povera.

content.text: The pasta water is not optional here. It is starchy enough to bind the oil into a light, glossy sauce that coats every strand. Have it ready before you start cooking the garlic, because everything moves quickly from that point.
Cook the spaghetti in a large saucepan of well-salted boiling water until 1 minute shy of al dente. Reserve at least 200ml of pasta water before draining.
While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium-low heat. Add the garlic and cook gently for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring often, until it is pale gold.
Add the chilli flakes and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the drained spaghetti and 100ml of the reserved pasta water. Toss vigorously over a medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes, adding more pasta water to loosen the sauce.
Remove from the heat. Add the parsley and toss again. Serve at once, with parmesan on the side if using.

items.cause: Cooked over too high a heat
items.fix: Start again with lower heat; garlic should go pale gold only.

items.symptom: Pasta is oily but not saucy
items.fix: Add more pasta water and toss until emulsified.
